bug_semantics: PATCH /api/customers/:id was reachable without an authenticated admin or customer session. The global API authorization middleware continued immediately for a public route, the endpoint-local middleware only parsed JSON, and updateCustomer trusted request.params.id as the target UUID and spread attacker-controlled request.body into the database update without checking ownership. A caller who knew a customer UUID could replace that customer's email and, after password hashing support was added, password, receive the updated record, and take over the account.
flaw_origin: The first exploitable state is the PR #168 member commit a2f514ad10073fb9ae164446f30205086151c095. Its parent already had the inert PATCH route definition but no updateCustomer handler. The commit added updateCustomer.js, which selects and updates a customer solely by the path UUID with no caller/owner check, and its BIC-time global auth treated a missing access property as public. Commit 4b97829de4acc674cd2282af3d2b61ec3416f72b later changed missing access to private but explicitly added access=public to this route, preserving rather than introducing the vulnerability. Commit efbb64dc5714feb92bba17ff82121523733fb39a later added hashing of a supplied password, strengthening the account-takeover consequence without originating the authorization flaw.
ai_marker: No AI marker in the BIC commit object. `git cat-file -p a2f514ad10073fb9ae164446f30205086151c095` shows both author and committer as `The Nguyen <6950941+treoden@users.noreply.github.com>` and the complete message is only `RESTful api implementation`; there is no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-tool trailer, or bot identity.
evidence: First-party issue https://github.com/evershopcommerce/evershop/issues/952 states that unauthenticated PATCH /api/customers/:id can overwrite email/password/profile fields, identifies route access=public, the auth middleware's unconditional next(), the body-parser-only local chain, the UUID-based update, and records maintainer @treoden's `Fixed in v2.2.1` comment.

Run `git show a2f514ad10073fb9ae164446f30205086151c095 -- packages/evershop/src/modules/customer/api/updateCustomer` in the validated clone. It creates `[context]bodyParser[auth].js`, payloadSchema.json, and updateCustomer.js; the handler loads `.where('uuid', '=', request.params.id)`, then updates the same UUID with `{...request.body, group_id: 1}` and performs no identity or ownership check.

Run `git show 'a2f514ad10073fb9ae164446f30205086151c095:packages/evershop/src/modules/auth/api/global/[jwtTokenVerify]auth.js'` and `git show a2f514ad10073fb9ae164446f30205086151c095:packages/evershop/src/modules/customer/api/updateCustomer/route.json`. At the BIC, auth says `Missing access property means public` and calls next when access is absent, while the route has PATCH /customers/:id and no access field.

Direct parent check: `git cat-file -e 4e518e617b76928656936e0048da852229acf24e:packages/evershop/src/modules/customer/api/updateCustomer/updateCustomer.js` fails because the handler is absent. The parent does contain route.json, but without a handler it cannot perform the vulnerable customer write. `git diff 4e518e617b76928656936e0048da852229acf24e a2f514ad10073fb9ae164446f30205086151c095 -- packages/evershop/src/modules/customer/api/updateCustomer` shows the first executable update implementation.

Provenance cross-check: `git log --all -S".where('uuid', '=', request.params.id)" -- packages/evershop/src/modules/customer/api/updateCustomer/updateCustomer.js` returns a2f514ad10073fb9ae164446f30205086151c095 as the origin; `git log -L 7,33:packages/evershop/src/modules/customer/api/updateCustomer/updateCustomer.js` traces the vulnerable UUID lookup back to that file-creation commit. The GitHub PR #168 commits endpoint lists a2f514ad10073fb9ae164446f30205086151c095 as a distinct member with parent 4e518e617b76928656936e0048da852229acf24e, so it is not a merge, move, release commit, or opaque squash requiring decomposition.

Run `git show 4b97829de4acc674cd2282af3d2b61ec3416f72b -- packages/evershop/src/modules/customer/api/updateCustomer/route.json 'packages/evershop/src/modules/auth/api/global/[userTokenVerify]auth.js'`. That later commit changes the default from missing=public to missing=private while adding explicit `access: public` to the update route; its immediate parent was already exploitable, so it is persistence, not the BIC.

At vulnerable tag v2.1.2, `git show v2.1.2:packages/evershop/src/modules/customer/api/updateCustomer/route.json` shows access public; `git show 'v2.1.2:packages/evershop/src/modules/auth/api/global/[getCurrentUser]auth.ts'` calls next for public routes; the endpoint directory contains only a JSON body parser before auth; and updateCustomer.js hashes a supplied password and updates by request.params.id without ownership verification.

Fix proof: `git show f92b832255102af8db796245db01e38ea70504e9 -- packages/evershop/src/modules/customer/api/updateCustomer/route.json` changes only `access` from `public` to `private`; its direct parent is 8861498694b46f944767c49cc03180a96b38aac3. With the existing global middleware, private routes require a current admin UUID, closing the unauthenticated path.

Release boundary: `git tag --contains a2f514ad10073fb9ae164446f30205086151c095 --sort=version:refname` lists every repository release tag from 1.0.0-rc.9 through v2.2.1. `git tag --contains f92b832255102af8db796245db01e38ea70504e9 --sort=version:refname` lists only v2.2.1. Peeled commits are 1.0.0-rc.9=bf223e71cb0f9037a9df055fa50e0073dcbc1dee, v2.1.2=e84e2ebe3320160b50904478180eecc3911d11af, and v2.2.1=89d09fbd200931daa892c59ee8e5866490788e4c. Route blobs are public in 1.0.0-rc.9 and v2.1.2 and private in v2.2.1, making v2.2.1 the first tagged fixed release in this history.

BIC-only AI check: `git cat-file -p a2f514ad10073fb9ae164446f30205086151c095` yields tree 99a31b5e935a409fc77d7f4e2afe479ac9e7e67e, sole parent 4e518e617b76928656936e0048da852229acf24e, human author/committer The Nguyen using the treoden noreply address, and a one-line message with no trailers or bot marker. No later commit, PR text, or fix metadata was used for the AI verdict.
reasoning: The route shell alone in 4e518e617b76928656936e0048da852229acf24e was not exploitable because no update handler existed. a2f514ad10073fb9ae164446f30205086151c095 is therefore the smallest public-history commit that completed the unauthenticated arbitrary-customer update path: it created both the unsafe handler and the BIC-time authorization behavior under which the access-less route was public. Later explicit-public configuration and password hashing preserve or amplify the same flaw. f92b832255102af8db796245db01e38ea70504e9 directly closes it by making the route private, and the first fixed release tag is v2.2.1. Because the BIC commit object contains a human identity and no permitted AI marker, the required BIC-only judgment is NOT_AI.
